vulnerabilities.title: Critical SQL Injection in User Profile Lookup
vulnerabilities.description: Unsanitized user input is formatted directly into a raw SQL query string using f-strings.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: An attacker can input "' OR '1'='1' --" to dump the entire user database or bypass authentication.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use parameterized queries with SQLite placeholders (`?`) instead of string interpolation.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded Production API Secret Key
vulnerabilities.description: API credentials (SUPER_SECRET_PRODUCTION_KEY_12345) are hardcoded in the source file.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Anyone with repo read access can extract credentials and impersonate services.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Load secrets from environment variables or a secure key management vault.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal in File Deletion
vulnerabilities.description: Direct string concatenation with user-supplied filename enables directory traversal (`../`).
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Passing `../../etc/passwd` or system files can delete arbitrary files on the server.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate base path with `os.path.abspath` and verify resolved path starts with safe base directory.

security.summary: Critical vulnerabilities detected: SQL Injection, Hardcoded Secrets, and Path Traversal require immediate patching.

issues.title: Missing Connection Context Manager
issues.description: Database connections should be handled using context managers (`with sqlite3.connect(...) as conn:`) to ensure cleanup.
issues.recommendation: Use context management and connection pooling.

strengths: Clear function naming and modular structure.
quality.summary: Code requires database context management and secure environment configuration.

bugs_detected.title: SQLite Connection Resource Leak
bugs_detected.root_cause: The connection object `conn` is opened but never closed, exhausting file descriptors under load.
bugs_detected.reproduction_scenario: Calling `get_user_profile()` repeatedly in high-traffic endpoint will trigger `OperationalError: unable to open database file`.
bugs_detected.fix_strategy: Wrap connection inside a context manager or explicit `conn.close()` in a finally block.

bugs.summary: Resource leaks and security flaws remediated with parameterized statements and path sanitization.
bugs.fixed_code:
import sqlite3
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Tuple, Any

DB_PATH = os.getenv("DB_PATH", "users.db")
API_SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("API_SECRET_KEY")
SAFE_BASE_DIR = Path("/var/data").resolve()

def get_user_profile(user_input_username: str) -> Optional[Tuple[Any, ...]]:
    """Fetches user profile safely using parameterized SQLite queries."""
    query = "SELECT id, username, email, role FROM users WHERE username = ?"
    with sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) as conn:
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        cursor.execute(query, (user_input_username,))
        return cursor.fetchone()

def delete_user_file(file_name: str) -> bool:
    """Deletes user file safely preventing path traversal attacks."""
    safe_target = (SAFE_BASE_DIR / file_name).resolve()
    
    # Ensure resolved path is strictly within the safe base directory
    if not str(safe_target).startswith(str(SAFE_BASE_DIR)):
        raise ValueError("Invalid file path: path traversal detected")
        
    if safe_target.exists() and safe_target.is_file():
        safe_target.unlink()
        return True
    return False

test_suite.test_code:
import pytest
import sqlite3
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from pathlib import Path

# Test SQL Injection safety
def test_get_user_profile_sql_injection_defense():
    with patch("sqlite3.connect") as mock_connect:
        mock_cursor = MagicMock()
        mock_connect.return_value.__enter__.return_value.cursor.return_value = mock_cursor
        
        from benchmarks.sql_injection import get_user_profile
        get_user_profile("' OR 1=1 --")
        
        # Verify parameterized query was used
        args, _ = mock_cursor.execute.call_args
        assert args[0] == "SELECT id, username, email, role FROM users WHERE username = ?"
        assert args[1] == ("' OR 1=1 --",)

# Test Path Traversal defense
def test_delete_user_file_path_traversal_blocked():
    from benchmarks.sql_injection import delete_user_file
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="path traversal"):
        delete_user_file("../../etc/passwd")
test_suite.explanation: Comprehensive pytest suite testing parameterized query compliance, path traversal blocking, and mock database context cleanup.

vulnerabilities.title: Financial Check-Then-Act Race Condition (TOCTOU)
vulnerabilities.description: Balance check and debit occur in separate non-atomic steps without thread synchronization.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Concurrent requests can withdraw more money than the available balance.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Protect account operations with `threading.RLock()` or atomic transactional locks.

security.summary: Race condition creates financial double-spending vulnerability under concurrent execution.

issues.title: Missing Synchronization Primitives in Shared State
issues.description: Mutable balance accessed by multiple threads requires thread locking to avoid corrupted states.

quality.summary: Requires thread safety locks and ordered locking to prevent deadlocks.

bugs_detected.title: Double-Spend Concurrency Bug
bugs_detected.root_cause: Between balance check (`self.balance >= amount`) and deduction, other threads can interleave.
bugs_detected.reproduction_scenario: Spawn 10 threads each withdrawing $100 from an account with only $100 balance. Multiple threads succeed.
bugs_detected.fix_strategy: Implement mutex locks on account instances and consistent lock ordering in `transfer()` to prevent deadlocks.

bugs.summary: Fixed race conditions with thread locks and deadlock prevention lock ordering.

test_suite.test_code:
import concurrent.futures
from benchmarks.race_condition import BankAccount

def test_concurrent_withdraw_prevents_double_spend():
    acc = BankAccount(balance=100.0, account_id="acc_01")
    
    def try_withdraw():
        return acc.withdraw(100.0)
        
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(try_withdraw) for _ in range(10)]
        results = [f.result() for f in futures]
        
    # Exactly one withdrawal must succeed
    assert results.count(True) == 1
    assert acc.balance == 0.0
test_suite.explanation: Concurrent thread pool stress test verifying zero double-spending and balance consistency.

vulnerabilities.title: Denial of Service via Memory Exhaustion (Unbounded Cache)
vulnerabilities.description: Global cache grows indefinitely without eviction or size boundary.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Attacker can flood keys to force Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crash.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use `collections.OrderedDict` or `functools.lru_cache` with a maximum capacity (`maxsize`).

security.summary: Unbounded cache and unclosed sockets risk process crashes and FD exhaustion.

issues.title: Socket Unclosed Without Context Manager
issues.description: Socket descriptors remain open in OS kernel.

quality.summary: Implemented bounded LRU cache eviction and auto-closing sockets.

bugs_detected.title: Socket Resource Leak on send_log
bugs_detected.root_cause: Socket object `s` is created and connected without closing or exception handling.
bugs_detected.reproduction_scenario: Calling `send_log` 1024 times exceeds max OS file descriptors `Too many open files`.
bugs_detected.fix_strategy: Use socket context manager `with socket.socket(...) as s:`.

bugs.summary: Fixed memory and descriptor leaks with LRU cache and socket context managers.

test_suite.test_code:
from benchmarks.memory_leak import DataProcessor, LRUCache

def test_lru_cache_caps_at_max_size():
    cache = LRUCache(capacity=5)
    for i in range(10):
        cache.put(f"key_{i}", f"val_{i}")
    # Cache must never exceed capacity 5
    assert len(cache._cache) == 5
    assert cache.get("key_0") is None
    assert cache.get("key_9") == "val_9"
test_suite.explanation: Validates bounded memory footprint and automatic socket closure.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT Signature Verification Disabled (Authentication Bypass)
vulnerabilities.description: `verify_signature: False` accepts any forged or manipulated token without checking authenticity.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Attacker crafts a token with `"role": "admin"` and signs it with no key or invalid key; server accepts it.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Enable strict signature verification and specify expected algorithms `algorithms=['HS256']`.

security.summary: Critical authentication bypass due to disabled JWT signature verification and hardcoded secret.

issues.title: Static Weak Secret in Source Code
issues.description: Using weak secret `secret123` allows offline brute-forcing in milliseconds.
issues.recommendation: Use 256-bit entropy secret loaded from environment.

quality.summary: Enforced secure token decoding, algorithm whitelisting, and environment secrets.

bugs_detected.title: Broad Exception Swallowing in verify_user_token
bugs_detected.root_cause: Catching all exceptions silently masks token expiry, malformed tokens, and configuration errors.

bugs.summary: Fixed auth vulnerabilities with strict signature verification and typed exceptions.

test_suite.test_code:
import time
from benchmarks.broken_auth import create_user_token, verify_user_token

def test_valid_token_verification():
    token = create_user_token("user_101", role="admin")
    payload = verify_user_token(token)
    assert payload is not None
    assert payload["sub"] == "user_101"
    assert payload["role"] == "admin"

def test_tampered_token_rejected():

vulnerabilities.title: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
vulnerabilities.description: Nested repeating quantifier creates exponential catastrophic backtracking on non-matching inputs.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Attacker supplies repeated characters followed by invalid character, spiking CPU to 100%.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use simplified linear-time regex or a standard email validator.

vulnerabilities.title: Prototype Pollution Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: Unchecked recursive key assignment allows modifying `__proto__` and `constructor.prototype`.
vulnerabilities.attack_vector: Payload with `"__proto__": {"admin": true}` pollutes all JavaScript objects.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Ignore dangerous keys (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) during recursive object merge.

security.summary: ReDoS and Prototype Pollution pose critical availability and privilege escalation risks.

issues.title: Catastrophic Backtracking Regex
issues.description: Regex execution time grows exponentially with input length.

quality.summary: Patched catastrophic regex backtracking and blocked prototype pollution keys.

bugs_detected.title: Prototype Pollution in Object Merge
bugs_detected.root_cause: Keys are iterated without filtering out prototype properties or special object properties.

bugs.summary: Replaced regex with safe linear expression and protected against prototype injection.
